chunks: Al-Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad al-Baṣrī narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from ʿAmr ibn Ziyād, from Mudrik ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام, who said:

When it is the Day of Resurrection, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will gather the people on a single plain, and the scales will be set down. Then the blood of the martyrs will be weighed alongside the ink of the scholars, and the ink of the scholars will outweigh the blood of the martyrs.

key_terms.الْمَوَازِينُ: the scales by which deeds and worth are weighed
key_terms.دِمَاءُ الشُّهَدَاءِ: the blood of the martyrs, symbolizing sacrifice in the way of Allah
key_terms.صَعِيدٍ وَاحِدٍ: a single plain on which humanity is assembled
key_terms.مِدَادُ الْعُلَمَاءِ: the ink of the scholars, symbolizing preserved and transmitted sacred knowledge
key_terms.يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection, when all people are gathered and judged

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the virtue of the scholars’ ink compared to the blood of the martyrs?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a scene from the Day of Resurrection in which deeds are weighed before Allah. It emphasizes the immense rank of sacred knowledge and the scholars whose learning and writing benefit religion, portraying their ink as outweighing even the blood of the martyrs.
